title: Recorder
summary: An alto recorder built only from the published measurements of one real baroque alto (a Bressan recorder of the Frans Brueggen collection, as tabulated by Jan Bouterse): the bore of its three joints, the thumb hole and six finger holes, the window, the labium and step, and the windway length. The windway height is not published for this instrument and is estimated from other altos. Four fingerings of the first register, F4, A4, Bb4 and B4 from Bouterse's table, are rendered as held notes at a pressure read from published register-jump thresholds, and as slow crescendos that choose no pressure at all. The scale and melody add G4, C5, D5, E5 and F5 from the American Recorder Society's alto chart, which names no recorder. C5 to F5 are blown at one player's measured pressures from Blanc's 2009 thesis, on a Zen-On Bressan alto with a machined aluminium chamfered head, not the maker's own; Blanc reports the makers Henri Gohin and Philippe Bolton judging the channel of those machined heads too low. Speaks; not graded on the site. It speaks, but it does not sound like a recorder yet: it leaves the first register at the lowest blowing pressures, sounds higher modes of the pipe, and comes back to the first register only above 270 to 390 Pa, where a real recorder has already jumped to its second. Listening only: screened recordings of recorders exist in the library (84 valid clips on 18 pitches from Bb4 to E6, from several instruments, sources and licences, none of this Bressan alto), but the grader's library is built from UIowa-named files and holds none of them, so no pair is graded and nothing here claims to match a real recorder.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing pressure through the viscous windway law with the published windway length, the published window length as the jet length and the window width as the flue width, acting on a connected duct network (one jet drives the whole graph)

the published bore of the head, middle joint and foot as equal-volume cylinders (the head's oval at its area-equivalent diameter), the thumb hole and six finger holes as chimney sections on ideal junctions (chimney height from the published outer diameter and the local bore), open or closed per the published fingerings, each open hole with its inner length (the Dubos-Dalmont law at its local bore), its matching length and its series length (Garcia Mayen et al. 2021, eqs. 12 and 10; the series length is taken off the bore on each side of the hole), and the bore closed by the block behind the window

the window as an acoustic mass from Ernoult and Fabre 2017's closed form (fitted to 444 finite-element windows) for the published 12.0 x 4.6 mm cut with parallel cheeks and the labium ramp, moved from their edge plane to the window centre, in place of a textbook end correction; the 3-D potential-flow solve of the same cut still runs as the comparison; the network keeps the window's channel only as a one-sample inlet line, so no 1-D line rings across a channel whose cross modes start at 13.5 kHz
hole 7 on the foot at a derived position (24 mm below the socket rim, bracket 18 to 30 mm), open in a1, b-flat1 and b1 as the published fingerings open it

breath as the gas in the bore: exhaled breath saturated with water at 27 C with its published 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 (dry), the woodwind breath law, read from the shared woodwind breath gas pack; it lowers every passive mode 19.1 to 19.3 cents below saturated air

fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the long bore sections (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops its memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, adbb97dbb and f78078db2)

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops the open holes and the foot's open end take the compact unflanged-pipe load instead, Garcia Mayen 2021, Eq. 14, with Silva et al. 2009, Eqs. 10-11, the foot's from ae3ef2d4e, and are still heard as baffled sources), plus the window, which radiates from the outer face of the same 3-D solve on the head's rigid outer cylinder (resistance from the cylindrical-harmonic series, its static mass by Kramers-Kronig and taken out of the window mass, a passive chain of parallel R-L-C cells fitted from 20 Hz to 24 kHz within 1.9 %) in place of an authored window loss (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops that radiation's memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, 27631e7a4)
deterministic oscillation: every held note sounds the same pitch and level for another jet seed, so it is a limit cycle and not a filtered seed

the start of every crescendo: each fingering begins in the first register of its pipe, at the lowest pressures. In that first-register span (the 100 ms windows within 100 cents of the first mode in the first 1.5 s, below 153 Pa) the crescendos sound f1 -31.7, a1 -65.9, b-flat1 -36.3 and b1 -55.4 cents of equal temperament on a1 = 409 Hz (median of those windows while the pressure rises), where the passive first modes are -50, -81, -48 and -64 cents, all with the bore gas at 27 C. The open holes' matching and series lengths moved those passive modes by 0, -1.3, -2.1 and -2.6 cents and these medians by 0, -4.2, -2.0 and -2.4. The a1 median also gained a window, 21 to 22: the one at 130 Pa, which read the pipe's third mode before and its first register after. Over the 21 windows in both renders, a1 moved -1.2 cents. That 27 C is the shared woodwind breath gas: the mean bore gas of a played mouth-blown woodwind, after Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969 and Fletcher and Rossing. A played Baroque flute measured with thermocouples along its bore averaged 27.3 C in a 20.6 C room (Soubeyran, Padfield, Gohin and Spohr). Bouterse's pitches for this alto were played in a 15 C room: f1 -14.8, a1 -34.8, b-flat1 -4.8 and b1 +5.2 cents on the same scale. Moved to the card's 27 C at 3 cents per degree, they depend on the bore temperature while Bouterse played. If the bore stayed at the room's 15 C, they become f1 +21.2, a1 +1.2, b-flat1 +31.2 and b1 +41.2, and the card's notes are 53, 67, 67 and 97 cents flat. If the bore was as warm as that flute's, they become -15.7, -35.7, -5.7 and +4.3, and the card's notes are 16, 30, 31 and 60 cents flat. Nothing is added to close it

breath noise at the flue: the `jet_noise` row (seed 14), a pressure source at the flue jet of rms 0.0013 of the jet's rho U^2 / 2 inside the Strouhal band St_h 0.045 to 0.115, open while the flue's Re_h = U h / nu is at least 700, which this flue (h 0.96 mm, the card's air) reaches at 72 Pa. Every page clears it: F4 held at 135 Pa (Re_h 959), A4 held at 210 Pa (Re_h 1196), and the four crescendos from 0.69 s, reaching 2021 at their 600 Pa peak. The constant, band and gate come from Verge's measurement of a flue jet at a labium with a 1 mm slit (PhD thesis, TU Eindhoven 1995, sec. 5.5), not determinable below Re_h about 1700, which this flue reaches at 424 Pa: the held pages and the crescendos' first 4.24 s take that gain below its measured range. The binary has no noise tap, so the noise's own level in the clip is not read apart
physics_missing: a graded comparison: screened recordings of recorders exist in the library (84 valid clips on 18 pitches from Bb4 to E6, from several instruments, sources and licences, none of this Bressan alto), but the grader's library is built from UIowa-named files and holds none of them, so no pair is graded and no claim of resemblance is made

register control: the loop leaves the first register at 78 to 117 Pa, far below the published first-register ceiling of a real Bressan alto (measured on an artificial mouth: F4 230, A4 305, Bb4 505, B4 490 Pa). It then sounds the pipe's second and third modes up to 220 to 350 Pa. Above 270 to 390 Pa it comes back to the first mode and holds it to the ramp's 600 Pa, where the real instrument has already jumped up; before the window radiation that return came only at 570 to 600 Pa, and not at all for b-flat1. So the held f1 and a1 (135 and 210 Pa) sound the pipe's second mode and are not recorder notes. The held b-flat1 and b1 (415 and 430 Pa) sound their first mode only through that return from above; before the window radiation they sounded their fourth mode. The same blowing, with the same island, reproduced a measured register ladder on the tin whistle, so the cause is in what is unknown for this windway (its height, shape and taper), not shown to be in the island

the windway: its height is not published for this alto (only its length) and is estimated from two other instruments; its curved, crescent-shaped opening, the direction of its roof, the chamfers and the taper of its section are unknown, and the recipe has a straight rectangular slit. The pressure-to-jet-speed map and every register claim depend on the height, and a sweep of the published bounds has not been made

labium offset: DERIVED, not measured. The published step and edge give the edge underside 0.27 mm on the bore side of the jet centreline at the estimated windway height, and the jet splits at the middle of the 0.25 mm face: +0.1455 mm on the pipe side (face ends +0.02 to +0.27 mm; the windway-height bounds move it from -0.225 to +0.425 mm); jet angle zero. With the gain-90 jet swinging 25 to 31 jet half-widths at the labium, this put H2 42 to 53 dB below H1 before the window radiation (36 to 70 dB across the face; the swing too was measured then). With the radiation, H2 is 58 to 75 dB below H1. So the even harmonics stay far weaker than on a measured Zen-On head: un-parity index +28 to +47 dB here (+23 to +31 before the radiation) against about -2 dB measured (Auvray et al. 2015, a comparison only)
the second and third registers: the thumb hole is a fully open or closed hole; the half-closed thumb hole that raises the register is not modelled, so only first-register fingerings are rendered

pitch: hole 7's position is derived, not measured (bracket 18 to 30 mm); the finger holes have no undercutting, and the closed holes no matching volume or series length (the open holes carry their inner, matching and series lengths, which are open-hole forms); the labium edge height is inherited from the unknown windway height (an edge at the bore or 1.25 mm above it moves every note by about +10 or -9 cents, passive); the measured bore is the tabulated maximum of a shrunken, slightly oval boxwood joint (the head taken at the oval's area-equivalent diameter, the midpoint of its published 0.2 to 0.4 mm)
the jet: the card is the repository's interim slot-jet card of a lattice rig, outside its Reynolds band; the displacement gain is the demonstrator value, not a measured amplification

a spectrum and attack like a real recorder: the held f1 and a1 are not first-register notes, b-flat1 and b1 reach their first register only from above (see register control), and no chiff or edge-tone noise is modelled

the gas beyond the breath law: the CO2 fraction is the published one for exhaled breath, not measured in a played recorder; no temperature gradient along the bore, and the published pitch was measured in rooms at 15 to 27 C (about 40 cents between them)
native verification beyond one fingering at two mechanics clocks and two jet seeds on a few files

Openings that hear each other: the open holes and the foot's open end radiate apart. Tried with every opening hearing every other free-field, after the travel time between them (`outlet_mutual free-field`), every page and scale or melody note with two or more holes open (the A4 held page; the A4, Bb4 and B4 crescendos; A4, Bb4, C5, D5, E5 and F5 in the stops) was refused before rendering, because with these loads the row is not passive: the real part of the openings' impedance matrix has a negative eigenvalue from the lowest frequencies up to 73 to 138 Hz with three openings, and up to 2.1 to 3.1 kHz with five to seven. The time step is not the cause: the exact free-field term with the loads' continuous form fails on the same notes. Each compact unflanged-pipe load's resistance falls short of a free-field monopole's by a share that grows with the square of frequency, and three or more openings in a line, closer together than a wavelength, radiate so nearly as one source that the matrix has less than that to spare. G4, with the foot and one hole open 78.2 mm apart, passes; it is not a page, so the row stays off the recorder

Openings that hear each other, weighted by their own radiation: tried with the free-field term between every pair of openings scaled by the square root of the two openings' own radiation resistances over a free-field monopole's (`outlet_mutual pritchard`; Pritchard 1960 as printed by Butler 2022, Eq. 1, with the geometric mean for unequal openings), which is passive with these loads by construction, every page and scale or melody note rendered. The row lowered the A4 held page, the A4, Bb4 and B4 crescendos by 0.7, 0.7, 0.4 and 0.2 c. A4 and B4 already sit flat of the recording, so the gap grew: 27.7 to 28.4 c on the A4 held page, 19.2 to 19.9 c on the A4 crescendo, 5.8 to 6.0 c on the B4 crescendo. Bb4 sits sharp and its gap shrank, 10.0 to 9.7 c, but the mean error of H2 to H12 against the recording grew, 15.07 to 15.27 dB. The mean error went 12.21 to 11.65 dB on the A4 held page, 9.936 to 9.941 dB on the A4 crescendo and 5.43 to 5.54 dB on the B4 crescendo. No page gains on both, so the row stays off. The half-space form of Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard (2013, Eq. 16), twice the free-field term, is set aside: with these unflanged loads it is not passive even for two openings

Separated flow at the openings: the flow leaving each open hole and the open end separates and loses its kinetic energy, a loss in series with each opening's own radiation (`opening_losses`, Δp = ρQ|Q|/(2(C_c A)²)). Tried with C_c 1 on every opening: the open end as Atig, Dalmont and Gilbert 2004 print it (C. R. Mécanique 332:299-304, Eq. 3, c_d = 2 for a thin-walled unflanged end), the side holes at the row's ceiling of 1, a loss 1.2 times the one Dalmont et al. 2002 print for a sharp-edged hole (Acta Acust. united Ac. 88:567-575, K_h = 0.5, as quoted by Szwarcberg et al. 2024, JASA, Sec. III.2.1, which is C_c 1.096): a C_c above 1 would be pressure recovery, which this row's full-head loss cannot represent. Every page rendered. The mean error of H2 to H12 against the recording grew on all six pages: 12.21 to 12.60 dB on the A4 held page, 9.61 to 9.81 dB on the F4 held page, and 9.94 to 12.34 dB, 15.07 to 16.67 dB, 5.43 to 12.12 dB and 11.94 to 12.44 dB on the A4, Bb4, B4 and F4 crescendos. The pitch moved by 0.5 c or less: the A4 held page went 0.5 c flatter, further from the recording; the A4 and B4 crescendos went 0.4 and 0.3 c sharper, closer to it; the Bb4 and F4 crescendos went 0.5 and 0.2 c sharper, further from it; the F4 held page moved less than 0.01 c. No page gains on both, so the row stays off
